title: Stage 8 — ORM, Migrations & Seeding
goal: Replace raw SQL with an ORM, version schema changes in migration files, and seed dev data reproducibly.
summary: Drizzle or Prisma on Express + SQLite — same routes, new data layer. Migrations and seeds you can replay.

pages.title: Schema view in the DB GUI

steps.title: Read the schema in a GUI

checkpoint.prompt: After running a migration, what should you verify in the DB GUI?

choices.text: Tables, columns, and foreign keys match what the migration defined
Only the number of Git commits
CSS variables in the frontend

checkpoint.explanation: The GUI schema view confirms the migration actually changed the database — don't assume success from logs alone.

checkpoint.prompt: You swap better-sqlite3 strings for Drizzle queries. What stays the same for the frontend?

choices.text: HTTP routes, URLs, and JSON response shapes
Nothing — the frontend must be rewritten
Only the HTML file names

checkpoint.explanation: ORMs change the data access layer inside handlers — not the public API contract.

choices.text: Describe one schema change step — committed to Git, applied in order
Contain the entire application source code
Be edited by hand on production only, never in Git

checkpoint.explanation: Migrations are versioned DDL steps. Teammates and CI replay the same history.

choices.text: Reproducible dev/test data (rows), not schema structure
Replacing migrations entirely
Storing user passwords in plain text

checkpoint.explanation: Migrations change structure; seeds insert sample rows you can wipe and re-run.

checkpoint.prompt: You run `npm run db:migrate` and add a column. Before merging the PR, you should…

choices.text: Refresh the DB GUI schema view and hit the API endpoint
Delete the database file and never check
Only read the migration filename

checkpoint.explanation: Verify schema in the GUI and behavior via Postman — same habit as Stage 5 and 6.

checklist.label: Drizzle or Prisma configured for Express + SQLite
At least GET/POST list routes use ORM instead of raw SQL strings
At least 2 migration files (initial schema + one alter)
Seed script populates dev data (`npm run db:seed` or equivalent)
Schema verified in DB GUI after migrations

questions.prompt: After a migration, the DB GUI schema view helps you…

choices.text: Confirm tables, columns, and FKs match what you intended
Deploy to production automatically
Replace the need for API tests

questions.explanation: Visual schema inspection catches typos and missed alters before they hit the team.

choices.text: Maps tables to objects and builds queries in your language
Replaces HTTP with WebSockets
Eliminates the need for a database

questions.explanation: ORMs sit between handlers and the DB — you still need routes and SQL concepts.

questions.prompt: Switching from raw SQL to Drizzle/Prisma, the frontend should…

choices.text: Keep calling the same URLs — only handler internals change
Switch to GraphQL immediately
Stop using fetch

questions.explanation: Swap the implementation layer; preserve the API contract.

choices.text: Applied in order — each change builds on the last
Applied randomly — order doesn't matter
Run only on the frontend server

questions.prompt: Seeding is different from migrating because seeds…

choices.text: Insert data rows for dev — safe to re-run after wipe
Change table structure permanently
Replace Git commits

questions.explanation: Migrations = DDL. Seeds = DML for sample data.
